claims.text: The starting elemental powders should have an oxygen content below 0.5 wt%.
High-energy milling for 20–30 hours will induce severe plastic deformation and homogenization.
The proposed SPS operating regime is 1100–1200 °C, approximately 50 MPa, heating above 200 °C/min, and a dwell below 5 minutes.
Processing under high-purity argon containing less than 10 ppm oxygen is required.
Cooling faster than 300 °C/min is part of the proposed SPS cycle.
The proposed milling and rapid SPS route will produce more than 98% relative density and suppress porosity.
The consolidated CoCrFeNiTi alloy will be a nanocrystalline solid solution dominated by FCC with minor BCC.
The proposed process will avoid nucleation of a Ti-rich brittle HCP phase.
The processed alloy will have a dislocation density above 5 × 10^14 m^-2.
The processed alloy will have a grain size below 1 μm.
Rapid thermal cycling will suppress grain growth.
Rapid SPS heating and cooling will kinetically suppress a diffusion-controlled transformation to an equilibrium HCP phase.
Milling-induced lattice strain and chemical homogeneity will favor an FCC solid solution in CoCrFeNiTi.
Cooling above 300 °C/min will quench and retain metastable FCC CoCrFeNiTi.
Rapid cooling prevents phase separation in HfNbTaTiZr and provides an analogous mechanism for CoCrFeNiTi.
The processed alloy will exhibit a Vickers hardness of 450–550 HV.
The predicted hardness will result from both grain refinement and solid-solution strengthening.
Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi is porous, single-phase FCC, and has hardness below 300 HV.
Oxygen above 0.6 wt% will cause oxide precipitation, HCP stabilization, brittle failure, and hardness above 600 HV.
The sintering strain rate can be controlled by matching rapid thermal expansion.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts that slow cooling promotes HCP formation, but the falsification rule treats observation of more than 10% HCP and brittle fracture in the deliberately slow-cooled control as falsifying rather than supporting that prediction.
